blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: The community sits above the Industrial Way / Progress Way industrial area on the valley floor; the City's Schweyey Road forcemain page places the mountain community above that industrial area, with sewage service along Schweyey Road for Chilliwack Mountain and portions of Industrial Way and Progress Way.
The residential streets are the mountain roads themselves — Chilliwack Mountain Road, Grandview Drive and Hillkeep Place at the top, and Sunrise Drive on the slopes.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Chilliwack Mountain Road corridor — Reflections @ Cedar Sky and Eagles Perch at the 43610–43680 stretch, Westpointe at 43777, Osprey Ridge at 43998 — and Sunrise Drive, where Maple Hills stands at 8590 Sunrise Drive. No apartment-condo street exists on the mountain in any source checked.

Nearby areas: Chilliwack Downtown and Chilliwack Proper West to the east, Little Mountain to the southeast, Fairfield Island across the river to the north, and the Lickman Road / Industrial Way corridor below the mountain to the west.
Chilliwack is CADREB ground — a page claiming an FVREB feed for this area is wrong.

Transit: no BC Transit route runs onto the mountain's residential streets; the closest listed service is route 59 Industrial – Downtown Chilliwack via the Lickman Park & Ride, with peak-period trips, and Highway 1 access is via the Lickman Road interchange south of the mountain.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: Strata vs fee-simple — the core distinction: four of the five counted complexes are confirmed strata; Westpointe's tenure is UNCONFIRMED and must be established on title before purchase. A strata townhouse buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, and gets a Form B package. A fee-simple townhouse buyer owns the lot outright: NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — municipal rules and any registered covenants/HOA only.

Hillside rules that hit townhouse owners directly: DPA D-2 covers the whole mountain, and a development permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks — the rule behind every addition, deck or rebuild conversation in a mountain strata.

Services: the City states the Schweyey Road forcemain provides sewage services for Chilliwack Mountain and portions of Industrial Way and Progress Way; service for a specific parcel or complex is not confirmed — verify water and sewer connection status for the specific lot.

Chilliwack property taxes: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% after August 4, 2026; additional taxes are levied for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rate.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: The mountain's townhouse stock now has names — the older research did not.

Lot size on the mountain is slope-driven, not just area-driven: in the SHR zone the minimum lot area rises from 360 m² in the lowest slope band to 990 m² in the highest — a lot's subdivision or rebuild potential depends on its measured slope.

There is no neighbourhood plan coming to change this: no Chilliwack Mountain plan appears in Schedule B (B1 to B7) of the Chilliwack 2050 OCP — the mountain is governed by the city-wide OCP and its hillside Development Permit Areas D-2 and D-5.

The park at the top is regional, not municipal: Hillkeep Regional Park (FVRD) is a nature reserve at the top of Chilliwack Mountain on Hillkeep Place, reached by Grandview Drive, with hiking trails and a viewing platform — the documented draw the mountainside complexes market against.

The nearest services are all off the mountain: Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre (9145 Corbould St), Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue), Chilliwack General Hospital (45600 Menholm Rd) and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre (#104 – 7955 Evans Road) — mountain households are car-dependent by design, with no bus route on the residential streets.
Drainage and dyking taxes ride on top of the municipal rate in Chilliwack — a small line on the tax notice that valley-floor systems explain, and one a mountain buyer still pays.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: Confirmed housing/land form: hillside residential lots carrying single-detached houses, with the housing form governed by the City's hillside development permit areas D-2 and D-5. Fee-simple is the default form: own title, no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.

Lot character from the hillside zones, as the bylaw states it: HR (Hillside Residential) Zone, minimum lot area 0.2 ha where served by a community water system and 0.4 ha for all other uses, minimum lot width 25 m; RH (Rural Hillside) Zone, minimum lot area 8 ha and minimum lot width 25 m; SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) Zone, minimum lot area set by the zone's slope table, starting at 360 m² for the lowest slope band and rising to 990 m² for the highest; SR (Suburban Residential) Zone, minimum lot area 650 m² where served by community water and community sanitary sewer, minimum lot width 17.5 m on the same services — all under City of Chilliwack Zoning Bylaw No. 5000. These are zone minimums, not a claim that every mountain lot is that size.

Slope is the lot character: in the SHR zone the minimum lot area rises with slope band (360 m² → 990 m²), so a lot's subdivision or rebuild potential depends on its measured slope, not just its area. Price buildable, permit-able area — not gross area and not view alone.
Tenure caution — Westpointe (43777 Chilliwack Mountain Road)

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: Chilliwack Mountain is a residential hillside neighbourhood in the City of Chilliwack, on the named mountain on the south side of the Fraser River, just west of Chilliwack Creek and west of the downtown core. Chilliwack is CADREB ground.

Residential streets are the mountain roads themselves — Chilliwack Mountain Road, Grandview Drive and Hillkeep Place at the top, and Sunrise Drive on the slopes. Highway 1 access is via the Lickman Road interchange south of the mountain, where BC Transit's Lickman Park & Ride sits.

Transit: no BC Transit route in the Chilliwack route list runs onto Chilliwack Mountain residential streets; the closest listed service is route 59 Industrial – Downtown Chilliwack to Cottonwood Mall via the Lickman Park & Ride, with peak-period trips.
Schools: no SD33 public school is located on Chilliwack Mountain itself; the schools physically in Chilliwack listed in the provincial school directory are all on the valley floor or in Sardis.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: Hillside permit rule — the governing lot rule on the mountain: Development Permit Area D-2 applies to Chilliwack Mountain, and a permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks. Budget the report and permit timing into any build, subdivision or renovation plan. DPA D-5 (Hillside Development) also covers the mountain.

Flood position: no mountain-specific floodplain statement was found in City material; the City's flood pages address the Fraser River dyke system on the valley floor below the mountain. A specific lot's flood status is UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked — slope diligence (D-2), not floodplain diligence, is the mountain's documented regime.

ALR rules (where a parcel is confirmed ALR — none confirmed in the research): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); BC Assessment farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel with the ALC first.

Chilliwack property taxes: City of Chilliwack property taxes for 2026 were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% late penalty after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% after August 4, 2026; municipal property tax rates are set by the City, and additional taxes are levied for drainage and dyking on top of the municipal rate.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chilliwack Mountain

items.t: Hillkeep Regional Park (FVRD) is the top-of-mountain anchor: a nature reserve at the top of Chilliwack Mountain on Hillkeep Place, reached by Grandview Drive via Hillkeep Place, with hiking trails and a viewing platform — open-space/park ground that shapes the mountain's top, not buildable lot area.

Everything else is down the hill: no City leisure centre, library branch, shopping centre or grocery store on the mountain was verified — the nearest leisure centre is Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre, 9145 Corbould St; the nearest library is Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue; the nearest grocery named in City material is Save-on-Foods Sardis, 6014 Vedder Road, in Sardis; Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Rd, and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #104 – 7955 Evans Road. Mountain land is bought for slope, view and trails, at the price of a drive for everything else.

Households here are car-dependent by design: no bus route serves the mountain's residential streets and the closest service is route 59 at the Lickman Park & Ride — factor access into lot value, especially on the upper roads in winter conditions (weather effect itself UNVERIFIED — the transit/access facts are as cited).

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Chilliwack Mountain?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Chilliwack Mountain?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Chilliwack Mountain?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Are the mountain's townhouses strata or fee-simple?
faq.a: Strata in four of five counted cases: Maple Hills is freehold strata LMS1735 and Osprey Ridge is freehold strata EPS8601 expressly, and Reflections and Eagles Perch publish strata fees in their listings. Westpointe's tenure is UNCONFIRMED — check title before assuming either way, because strata means a Form B and monthly fees, and fee-simple means neither.
If it is a bylaw, only a 55+ threshold is lawful in BC (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2). Read the bylaws before marketing or buying on that basis.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Maple Hills townhouse? The directory says rentals are not allowed.
faq.a: That directory line reflects a rental-restriction bylaw, and rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022 — long-term rentals cannot be banned by bylaw, though short-term rentals can still be restricted. Confirm the current registered bylaws on the Form B.

faq.q: How old is Maple Hills, really?
faq.a: Sources disagree by phase: building summary 2004, directory 2005, individual listings 1994 and 2002. It is a phased complex; the Form B and strata plan for the specific unit settle its phase year.

faq.q: What does the hillside permit area mean for me as an owner?
faq.a: DPA D-2 covers the whole mountain: a development permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment is required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks. Budget the report and permit timing into any build or major renovation plan, and expect the strata to apply the same lens to common-property work.

faq.q: What land actually trades on Chilliwack Mountain?
faq.a: Fee-simple hillside lots carrying (or able to carry) single-detached houses. No bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: How big can a mountain lot be — and how small can I split it?
faq.a: By zone and slope: HR 0.2 ha on community water / 0.4 ha otherwise (width 25 m); RH 8 ha; SHR 360 m²–990 m² by slope band; SR 650 m² on full services (width 17.5 m). The SHR slope table decides — get the slope measured.

faq.q: What permit do I need before I subdivide or build?
faq.a: A DPA D-2 development permit with a geotechnical hazard and slope assessment — required before subdivision, construction, land clearing or earthworks anywhere in the permit area, which covers the mountain.
